text: Sixty-eight year old female, sudden left-sided weakness, husband says she was normal at one forty.
notes: Deficit only, no exam: no RACE items and no complaint.chief. 'Normal at' counts as LKW; only the LKW clause is family.

text: 58 yom c/o crushing substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm, started 40 minutes ago while shoveling snow.
Medic 14 to Valley Medical, we're en route with a stroke alert, ETA eight minutes.
notes: 'Stroke alert' is an alert type, not a stated complaint, so no complaint.chief. 'Medic 14' is the unit number.

text: On exam she's got a mild right facial droop, right arm drifts, right leg holds fine, no gaze deviation, she's following commands and her speech is clear.
notes: Explicit exam. 'Following commands, speech is clear' → aphasia_agnosia 0. Abnormal findings described in words are also listed as deficits (presence-scored).

text: 86 yof, ground level fall, caregiver found her on the bathroom floor this morning, unknown down time.
notes: Guide maps 'found on the floor' to onset_witnessed=false; applied although this is a fall call (the key is not restricted by call type). Caregiver → family per §3.

text: 67 yom, COPD exacerbation, sats 84 percent on room air, RR 32, tripoding with pursed lip breathing.
She was totally fine when I talked to her at 9 am, then her neighbor called me and said she couldn't get her words out.
speaker: daughter
notes: Daughter on mic → LKW is family. The speech deficit is the neighbor's report relayed by the daughter → bystander. Reported deficit, not an exam → no RACE aphasia item.

text: D-stick reads 38, patient is responsive to voice only, cool and diaphoretic.
RACE is, uh, face two, arm two, leg one, gaze one, aphasia two, so total of eight.
notes: RACE total is not a key. Numeric scores only, so no deficit phrases.

text: It feels like an elephant is sitting on my chest, it started when I was walking the dog, maybe half an hour ago?
speaker: patient
notes: Patient on mic states the complaint (presence-scored). Onset is hedged ('maybe ... ?') → no symptom.onset.

text: Copy, meeting you there.
Patient says she tripped over the dog and fell, denies hitting her head, denies any loss of consciousness.
notes: Symptom denials give no facts.

text: seventy four yom slurred speech in right sided weakness wife found him like this in the recliner
notes: ASR slip 'in' for 'and'. 'Found him like this' → onset_witnessed false; that clause comes from the wife → family. No exam → no RACE.

text: Nursing home patient, 91 yof, temp 101.8, heart rate 118, BP 88 over 50, resps 24, sats 90 percent on two liters nasal cannula, skin warm and flushed, foley bag is cloudy, we're headed to Mercy General, ETA twelve.
notes: Temp has no unit but 101.8 can only be Fahrenheit → 38.8 °C. Cloudy foley bag is a patient finding, not a scene note.

text: Husband thinks maybe she was okay around eleven last night, but he went to bed early so he's not sure.
notes: Hedged LKW ('thinks maybe', 'not sure') → no fact.

text: BP one forty two over eighty eight, pulse one oh four, resps twenty, sats ninety six on room air.
Sixty-one yof, c/c altered mental status, confused and disoriented to time and place, sugar one twenty two, no diabetic history.
Left facial droop, left arm drift, eyes deviated to the right, last known well 10 pm per son.
notes: Medic-observed findings without the word 'exam': unqualified 'facial droop' → facial 2 (§4), 'drift' → arm 1, deviation → gaze 1. Only the LKW clause is family.

text: Obvious deformity to the right hip, shortened and externally rotated, CMS intact distally.
notes: Injury exam findings; no key covers them and none is a stated complaint.

text: He was fine at dinner, uh, six thirty, and then he just slumped over at the table, I saw the whole thing.
speaker: son
notes: 'Slumped over' is an event, not a neuro deficit phrase.

text: He's used his ProAir like four times since dinner and it's not doing anything, he can barely talk.
speaker: mother
notes: ProAir → albuterol. 'Can barely talk' here is dyspnea, not a stroke deficit.

text: Pressure's one sixty over, sorry, one sixty-eight over ninety-four.
notes: Restart/correction: only the final 168/94 is labeled.

text: She's got weakness in the right arm and leg, and her speech is kind of garbled.
notes: Weakness without a drift/lift description and 'garbled' speech are deficits only; no RACE grade can be assigned.

text: She's allergic to shellfish and she had shrimp at dinner, her lips started swelling fifteen minutes ago.
speaker: husband
notes: Lip swelling is the presenting problem → complaint.chief (presence-scored).

text: Can you grab the stair chair and the drug box off the rig?
Pt denies blood thinners, NKDA, home meds are lisinopril and Lipitor, no head strike.
notes: Attribution scope: 'denies' governs only the blood-thinner clause; NKDA and the med list are unattributed → medic.

text: He took two of his nitro before you got here and it didn't help at all.
speaker: wife
notes: Home nitro taken before EMS arrival counts as a medication taken.

text: GCS 14, E4 V4 M6, pupils PERRL, c-collar applied.
notes: Only M6 gives gcs_motor; total GCS is not a key; no ACVPU letter inferred from GCS.

text: RACE five, um, face one, arm two, leg one, no gaze deviation, aphasia one.
notes: Items sum to the stated total of 5.

text: Wife says he's been short of breath for three days, worse tonight, and he ran out of his home oxygen yesterday.
notes: Running out of home O2 is history, not a vitals.on_oxygen statement.

text: He's a type one diabetic, takes Lantus at night and Humalog with meals, and he skipped dinner tonight.
speaker: wife

text: BP 210 over 110, correction, 201 over 110, heart rate 88, glucose 132.
She tripped on the curb and fell and hit her head on the sidewalk, but she never passed out.
speaker: bystander
notes: Bystander on mic → bystander role. One complaint fact (presence-scored).

text: Hx of MI with two stents, takes Plavix, metoprolol and Lipitor, allergic to morphine.
notes: Plavix (clopidogrel) is an antiplatelet, not in the guide's anticoagulant list → no meds.anticoagulant.

text: last known well 2 30 per daughter and daughter says she takes elequis
notes: ASR: '2 30' = 2:30, 'elequis' = Eliquis → apixaban.

text: BGL was 42, gave an amp of D50, recheck is 156, now A and O times four.
notes: Two sequential readings (a trend, not a correction) → both labeled. D50 given by EMS is an intervention, not a patient medication.

text: uh were gonna package her up and move now my partners driving
notes: ASR: 'were' for 'we're', 'partners' for 'partner's'.

text: Arm score is two, she can't lift the right arm at all, leg is a one.
Facility nurse says she's been more confused than baseline since yesterday, foley in place, urine cloudy and foul smelling.
notes: Facility nurse is a caregiver who knows the baseline, so family (guide §3). 'More confused than baseline' = new confusion → C; captured as consciousness, not complaint.chief.
adjudication: facility nurse = caregiver = family (guide §3 update); no complaint when the finding is captured by a structured key

text: BP one ten over seventy, uh, wait, one oh two over seventy, heart rate one eighteen, skin pale cool and clammy.
Placed on CPAP at 10, sats coming up to 92, wet crackles in all fields.
notes: CPAP treated as supplemental oxygen; '10' is the CPAP pressure, not liters or a vital.

text: Maybe a slight droop on the left side of her face, hard to tell with her dentures out.
notes: Hedged finding → no RACE facial and no deficit.

text: fifty two year old female chest tightness and nausea since three a m very diaphoretic
notes: ASR: 'a m' = am.

text: Bystanders say she seized for about two minutes, she's postictal now, only responding to voice.
notes: The seizure report is the bystanders'; current responsiveness is the medic's observation.

text: No facial droop, arms and legs are strong with no drift, speech is normal, eyes midline.
notes: Normal exam → all RACE items 0; no deficits.

text: glucose 5 hundred and 12 pt says he ran out of his metformin last week
notes: ASR: '5 hundred and 12' = 512. Ran out of metformin: still his prescribed medication → included in meds.list.

text: Twelve lead done at fourteen thirty two, ST elevation in two, three and aVF, I'll attach it to the ED report.
notes: Attachment is only intended (future) → no ecg.attached. Spoken 24-hour time written as 14:32.

text: Pt is on Lovenox shots since his knee replacement, lac to the forehead, bleeding controlled.
notes: 'Lac to the forehead' is an exam finding, not a stated complaint.

text: Change of plans, Mercy's on stroke divert, we're going to St. Joseph's instead, new ETA twenty two.
notes: Mercy is mentioned only as diverting → not the destination.

text: She takes Xarelto and something for her thyroid, she's allergic to penicillin, and she fell getting out of the tub.
speaker: husband
notes: Unnamed thyroid medication is not labeled.

text: Stroke alert, 81 year old male, LKW 0630, RACE of 7, he's on Eliquis per the wife, BP 196 over 104, glucose 118, going to Regional, ETA 14 minutes, please have CT ready.
notes: RACE total without item scores → no RACE items. 'Stroke alert' → no complaint. LKW kept in the spoken 24-hour form '0630'. Only the Eliquis clause is family.
adjudication: LKW kept as spoken '0630'; scorer now normalizes times (colons, leading zeros)

text: seven year old male audible weezing sats ninety one percent heart rate one forty mom thinks he might have a peanut allergy
notes: Hedged allergy ('thinks he might have') → no allergies fact. Wheezing is an exam finding, not a complaint. ASR: 'weezing'.

text: She's usually alert and chatty, but today she only opens her eyes when you pinch her.
speaker: caregiver
notes: Baseline 'usually alert' is not the current state → not A. Caregiver on mic → family.

text: Right arm drifts down in about five seconds, left arm holds without drift.
notes: Worse arm scored: drift → 1.

text: HR 42, sinus brady, BP 84/50, pale and diaphoretic, A&O x3.
notes: A&O (any x-count stated here) → A per §4.

text: Witness says he fell off the ladder, maybe ten feet, and he's not sure if the guy's on blood thinners.
notes: Uncertain blood-thinner status → no anticoagulant fact (not 'none').

text: Leg, uh, she can't lift the left leg off the bed at all, and the arm's the same.
notes: 'The arm's the same' explicitly equates the arm finding → arm 2.

text: Allergic to sulfa and codeine, full code per the daughter.
notes: 'Per the daughter' governs only the code-status clause.

text: Resps are, um, twenty eight, twenty eight and labored, sat's eighty nine on two liters nasal cannula, gonna bump him to a non-rebreather.
Eyes are looking to the right, and she doesn't recognize her left arm, doesn't even know she's weak.
notes: Recognizes neither arm nor deficit → aphasia_agnosia 2.

text: Stroke team's been notified, they'll meet us in CT.
Sugar's forty-eight, uh, no, eighty-four, I read it upside down.
sixty two yof a phasic right arm is flaccid polst on the fridge says dnr
notes: ASR split 'a phasic' = aphasic → aphasia_agnosia 2; 'flaccid' → arm 2. Code status read off the POLST by the medic → medic.

text: Describes it as pressure, eight out of ten, doesn't radiate, denies shortness of breath or nausea.
notes: No complaint noun is stated ('it' is unspecified); pain scale is not a key; denials give nothing.

text: MVC, restrained driver, moderate front end damage, airbags deployed, self-extricated and ambulatory on scene.
notes: Vehicle observations are scene notes. 'MVC' is the mechanism of injury, labeled as complaint.chief like 'fall' (guide §4).
adjudication: mechanism of injury (MVC) counts as complaint.chief, like 'fall' (guide §4 update)

text: Temp one oh three point one tympanic, pulse one thirty, pressure's soft, eighty over, no, ninety over sixty.
notes: 103.1 °F → 39.5 °C. BP restart: only 90/60.

text: Wife witnessed the onset, says he dropped his coffee cup at 7:15 and couldn't get a word out.
notes: 7:15 is stated as when symptoms began → symptom.onset; not copied into stroke.lkw (that would be inference). Reported deficit → no RACE.

text: Satting 88 on 4 liters, correction, 6 liters, still 88.
notes: Correction is to the flow rate, which has no key.

text: Unresponsive, GCS 3, sugar 29.
notes: GCS 3 is a total; M1 is not stated → no gcs_motor.

text: daughter says she's been dragging her left leg and dropping things with her left hand sense this morning
notes: ASR: 'sense' = since. Reported deficits, no exam → no RACE.

text: Mom's on Coumadin and she hit her head pretty hard on the nightstand.
speaker: daughter
notes: Head strike is the presenting problem → complaint.chief (presence-scored).

text: Twelve lead is attached to the report, time on it is 10:47.
No known allergies, meds are Synthroid, Norvasc and a baby aspirin daily.
notes: Aspirin is not an anticoagulant → no meds.anticoagulant.

text: ETA is 15, um, make that 18 minutes, traffic's backed up on 101.
notes: '101' is a highway.

text: seventy nine year old woman with right sided facial droop and aphasia on cumadin for a fib lkw nine fifteen
notes: ASR: 'cumadin' = Coumadin → warfarin. Unqualified 'facial droop' → 2; unqualified 'aphasia' treated like 'aphasic' → 2.

text: Temp ninety five point four, she was on the floor all night, room air sat ninety one.
notes: 95.4 °F → 35.2 °C. 'On the floor all night' does not say found/witnessed → no onset_witnessed.

text: Eighty two, sorry, seventy two year old male, right facial droop, slurred speech.
notes: Age corrected to 72. Slurred speech is not an aphasia grade.

text: I don't take any blood thinners, and I'm not allergic to anything.
speaker: patient

text: shortness of breath started an hour ago history of chf takes lasix and eloquis
notes: ASR: 'eloquis' = Eliquis → apixaban; Lasix → furosemide.

text: Patient says he took his insulin this morning but hasn't eaten anything, he's a little confused but answering questions.
notes: 'Patient says' covers the insulin/eating clause; 'a little confused' is the medic's observation → medic.

text: 34 year old female, c/o lower right abdominal pain since yesterday, vomiting times three, temp ninety nine point six.
Numbness and tingling in her right hand and face, started twenty minutes ago.
facts: numbness and tingling in right hand and face
notes: Sensory deficit only → no RACE item.

text: Neighbor says he's been drinking since noon and fell off the porch steps.
notes: 'Since noon' refers to drinking, not symptom onset.

text: Engine 6 on scene, one patient, requesting ALS.
Found down by the neighbor this morning, last seen normal at 10 pm per the neighbor.
Heart rate one twenty, correction, one ten, still in a fib.
Temp one oh two point four, resps twenty six, sats ninety three on room air, crackles in the right base.
Son says she's been vomiting for two days, now she's unresponsive, sugar reads HI on the meter, breathing deep and rapid.
notes: Meter 'HI' is not a number → no glucose. 'Now she's unresponsive' is the medic's current observation.

text: She passed out in the checkout line, the cashier thinks she's diabetic, maybe on insulin, but isn't sure.
notes: Hedged history ('thinks', 'maybe', 'isn't sure') → no meds.list.

text: Pupils equal, grips unequal, weaker on the right, no other deficits noted.
notes: Grip strength is not a RACE item → no RACE.

text: Wife thinks his sugar was around sixty earlier but she's not sure, he's awake and talking now, A&O x4.
notes: Hedged earlier glucose → no glucose fact.

text: C-collar on, sats ninety eight on a non-rebreather, resps twenty four and shallow.

Stroke scale, facial palsy is, um, a one, mild, arm and leg both zero, no gaze deviation, speech is slurred, she's on Pradaxa per her daughter, sugar is ninety four, BP one seventy eight over ninety, and she's A&O times four.
notes: Slurred speech (dysarthria) is neither 'normal speech' nor aphasia → no aphasia_agnosia item. Only the Pradaxa clause is family.

text: Patient states he took two baby aspirin at home, didn't touch the pain.
Gave 324 of aspirin chewed and one nitro sublingual, pain's down to a five.
notes: Drugs given by EMS are interventions, not the patient's medications → no meds.list.

text: LKW two thirty, sorry, correction, two fifteen per husband.
Wife is showing me his out-of-hospital DNR, it's signed and dated, he's comfort care.
notes: The medic reads the document → medic, not family. 'Comfort care' is not a separate code_status value.

text: transporting emergent too good sam eta eleven
notes: ASR: 'too' = to.

text: Speech is fine, face symmetric, no drift in either arm, but the left leg drifts down and hits the bed.
notes: Leg lifts then drifts to the bed → 1 (drift), not 2 (can't lift).

text: Lights and sirens to Regional, we're about ten minutes out, can you have a bed ready?
notes: 'About' is the routine approximation of an ETA, not a hedge of the fact → labeled (contrast v1_015, v1_091).
